title: pvSpatioTemporalHarmonicsUniformGrid
body:
## pvSpatioTemporalHarmonicsUniformGrid

Generates image data (a uniform grid with spacing 1 over WholeExtent) with a time-dependent point array "SpatioTemporalHarmonics" = Σ A·sin(ω·t + k·x + φ), summed over the listed harmonics, at each listed time step. The ParaView defaults give four harmonics and 20 time steps over one 2π period, so the animation loops. Use it to test temporal filters, animation and time-dependent exports with a known analytic field; use pvWavelet for a static analytic volume.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- Point coordinates equal the grid indices (spacing 1), so wave vectors are per index unit.
- Schemaxis generates this source from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for it, so inspect the output before relying on it.

Native constructor: `SpatioTemporalHarmonicsUniformGrid`. Identity: `sources/SpatioTemporalHarmonicsSource`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

No connected inputs (source/resource).


### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Harmonics` | This property defines the harmonics that will be computed and summed on each point. By default, it generates harmonics in each direction, with parameters adapted to the default extent. Complete tuples of 6 values. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1]` |
| `TimeStepValues` | This property specifies the timestep values to generate. When generating a range, make sure to remove the max value for the loop to avoid time value duplication (0 == 2*Pi). By default, it generates 20 timesteps from [0;2*Pi[ for data loop. | `{"items":{"maximum":6.2832,"minimum":0.0,"type":"number"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[0.0]` |
| `WholeExtent` | The six values in the property indicate the X, Y, and Z extent of the output data. The first two numbers are the minimum and maximum X extent; the next two are the minimum and maximum Y extent; and the final two are the minimum and maximum Z extent. The numbers are inclusive, so values of -10, 10, -10, 10, -10, 10 indicate that the dimensions of the output will be 21 x 21 x 21. | `{"items":{"type":"integer"},"maxItems":6,"minItems":6,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1,1,1,1]` |
